thread.title: Roku: These Bulls Call the Company ‘Under-Appreciated’

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Roku: These Bulls Call the Company ‘Under-Appreciated’
text:
Photo: courtesy of Roku By David Marino-Nachison Sept. 4, 2018 10:48 a.m. ET Roku (ROKU) is “swimming with much bigger fish” in the streaming video business, but there’s room for multiple players to win, according to new research.
Guggenheim Securities on Monday started coverage of the Barron’s Next 50 company with a “buy” rating and a $74 price target that's 19% above current levels and nearly 30% higher than Factset’s mean target. (Their target is the highest tracked by FactSet.)
The shares, up about 20% in 2018, were ahead nearly 3% in Tuesday morning trading.
Newsletter Sign-up “At its current price both management’s stated initiatives and potential expansion opportunities are underappreciated,” Guggenheim wrote. “While the digital industry is competitive, we believe Roku has unique technology and usage assets and is an attractive pure-play on a compelling secular trend.”
Roku has positioned itself to benefit broadly from the shift to digital television , selling devices that can stream video from a number of services, licensing its technology to television makers, and offering its own ad-supported streaming service . (It’s also getting into smart speakers .)
Illustration: Guggenheim “We see Roku as positioned for success because it provides an improved value proposition for multiple stakeholders,” Guggenheim’s analysts wrote. “We believe consumers like the simplicity, breadth of content, and pricing options that Roku provides. Businesses benefit from Roku’s scale in targeted video advertising and infrastructure partnerships. [And] manufacturers benefit from utilizing the efficient and independent Roku operating system.”
The competition—with companies including Amazon.com (AMZN), Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google , and Apple (AAPL)—is “the most significant investor concern,” Guggenheim wrote.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 But Roku’s devices have a strong brand and are good quality, according to the analysts, and there’s “ample growth opportunity for multiple platforms” to go after ad-supported streaming revenue.
Overseas growth and the possibility of an acquisition by a company ”that would value the existing user base and platform as underappreciated,” are also reasons for possible share price growth, they wrote.
